(Lataif)
As for His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, it is a declaration of tawhid by Him concerning Himself, and a command to the addressee to affirm His oneness.
So when the servant says ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, he has affirmed Allah's oneness with what He affirmed about Himself, and he brings the word "say" to confirm this meaning, that he is a pure conveyor, one who speaks what he was commanded to say, and Allah knows best.
This differs from His saying: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾ and ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾, for these are a pure command to make the seeking of refuge, not a conveyance of a statement. For Allah does not seek refuge from anyone, and that would be impossible for Him. By contrast, ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ is a report about His oneness, and He, glorified is He, reports about Himself that He is the Single, the One. So reflect on this subtle point, and Allah is the One whose help is sought.
His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿He neither begets nor is He begotten﴾ is for the perfection of His self-sufficiency (samadiyyah),
﴿and there is none comparable to Him, anyone﴾, for His singularity in absolute perfection, in which no other shares with Him.
(Fasl)
When the polytheists asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the reality of his Lord, glorified is He: "Of what is He?", Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him, anyone.﴾
For this reason, when Pharaoh asked Moses about the reality of his Lord, saying: ﴿And what is the Lord of the worlds?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 23], Moses answered him: ﴿The Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them﴾.
Since humans have no access to the reality of His essence, He guided them to Himself through His affirmative attributes, such as His being Samad, and through His negative attributes that imply affirmation, such as His being "He neither begets nor is He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him, anyone." He did not leave them any path to knowing the essence and the true nature.
(Fasl)
"A man asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying: 'I love the surah ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾.' He said: 'Your love for it has admitted you into Paradise.'"
In another wording: "Inform him that Allah loves him."
"A man said to the Prophet ﷺ: 'O Messenger of Allah, I do not have anything with which to marry.' He said: 'Do you not have with you ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾?'
He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'It is a third of the Qur'an.'
He said: 'Do you not have ﴿Say: O you disbelievers﴾?'
He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'It is a quarter of the Qur'an.' He said: 'Do you not have ﴿When the earth is shaken﴾?'
He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'It is a quarter of the Qur'an.'
He said: 'Do you not have ﴿When the help of Allah comes﴾?'
He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'It is a quarter of the Qur'an.'
Do you not have the Verse of the Throne?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'It is a quarter of the Qur'an.' He said: 'Marry, marry, marry,' three times."
Ahmad narrated it.
From Abdullah ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ heard a man supplicating and saying: 'O Allah, I ask You, by my testifying that You are Allah, there is no god but You, the One, the Eternal Refuge, who neither begets nor is begotten, and there is none comparable to Him, anyone.' He said: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, he has asked Allah by His Greatest Name, which when He is called upon by it, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives.'"
At-Tirmidhi said: "A sound hadith."
This is seeking a means to Allah through His oneness, the witness of the supplicant to His unity, and the affirmation of His attributes indicated by the name al-Samad. It is, as Ibn 'Abbas said: "The Knowing whose knowledge is perfect, the Powerful whose power is perfect."
In another report from him: "He is the Lord (al-sayyid) in whom all kinds of lordship are perfected."
Abu Wa'il said: "He is the Lord whose lordship has reached its end."
Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "He is the one perfect in all His attributes, His acts, and His words, and the negation of likeness and resemblance from Him by His saying: ﴿and there is none comparable to Him, anyone﴾."
This is the summary of the creed of the People of the Sunnah, and seeking a means through belief in this and testifying to it is the Greatest Name.
(Fa'ida)
Among the occasions for sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ is upon entering the house.
Mentioned by the hafiz Abu Musa al-Madini.
He related with regard to it, from the hadith of Abu Salih ibn al-Muhallab, from Abu Bakr ibn Imran, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas ibn al-Walid told me, 'Amr ibn Sa'id told me, Ibn Abi Dhi'b told us, Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan told me, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said:
A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and complained to him of poverty and the straitness of living. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"When you enter your house, greet (with salam), whether or not anyone is in it, then send blessings upon me, and recite ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ once."
The man did so, and Allah opened up provision for him until he was bestowing upon his neighbours and relatives.
(Fasl)
The jurists have differed as to which of the two prayers is more emphasized: the Sunnah of Fajr or the Witr? There are two opinions. The preference cannot be determined by the jurists' disagreement about the obligation of Witr, for they have also disagreed about the obligation of the Sunnah of Fajr. I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya say: "The Sunnah of Fajr serves as the beginning of the work, and Witr is its conclusion. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ would pray the Sunnah of Fajr and Witr with the two surahs of sincerity (al-Ikhlas), which together comprise the tawhid of knowledge and action, the tawhid of recognition and intention, and the tawhid of belief and purpose." End of quote.
So the surah ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ comprises the tawhid of belief and recognition, and what must be affirmed for the Lord, exalted is He, of oneness (ahadiyyah), which negates any sharing in any way whatsoever, and of self-sufficiency (samadiyyah), which affirms for Him all attributes of perfection that are never touched by any deficiency, and the negation of begetting and being begotten, which is a necessary consequence of self-sufficiency, His independence and His oneness, and the negation of equal (kufu'), which implies the negation of likeness, resemblance and comparison. Thus this surah includes the affirmation of every perfection for Him, the negation of every deficiency from Him, the negation of affirming any like or equal to Him in His perfection, and the negation of any partner whatsoever. These foundations are the comprehensive principles of scientific doctrinal tawhid, which sets its adherent apart from all sects of misguidance and polytheism. For this reason it equals a third of the Qur'an, for the Qur'an revolves around report (khabar) and injunction (insha'), and injunction is of three kinds: command, prohibition, and permission.
Report is of two kinds: a report about the Creator, exalted is He, His names, attributes and rulings, and a report about His creation. So the surah ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ purified the report concerning Him, His names and His attributes, and thus it equals a third of the Qur'an, and it purified its reciter who believes in it from scientific polytheism, just as the surah ﴿Say: O you disbelievers﴾ purified from practical, volitional, intentional polytheism. Since knowledge precedes action, and it is its leader, guide and driver, and the judge over it and the one who places it in its stations, the surah ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ equals a third of the Qur'an.
The hadiths on this nearly reach the level of being mass-transmitted (mutawatir). And ﴿Say: O you disbelievers﴾ equals a quarter of the Qur'an. The hadith on this in at-Tirmidhi, from the narration of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, traced to the Prophet: "﴿When it is shaken﴾ equals half the Qur'an, ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ equals a third of the Qur'an, and ﴿Say: O you disbelievers﴾ equals a quarter of the Qur'an."
Al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak and said: its chain is sound.
Since practical, volitional polytheism prevails over souls because of their following their desires, and many of them commit it knowing its harm and falsehood, because of the worldly aims they gain from it, and removing and uprooting it from them is harder and more difficult than uprooting and removing scientific polytheism, because the latter is removed by knowledge and proof, and its bearer cannot know a thing other than as it is, unlike the polytheism of intention and purpose, for its bearer commits what knowledge indicates to be false and harmful, because of the dominance of his desire and the control of the power of lust and anger over his soul. Thus in the surah ﴿Say: O you disbelievers﴾, which includes the removal of practical polytheism, there came emphasis and repetition that did not come in the like of it in the surah ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾.
Since the Qur'an is in two halves: one half concerning the world, its rulings, its related matters, and the events occurring in it from the acts of the responsible and others, and one half concerning the Hereafter and what occurs in it, and since the surah ﴿When it is shaken﴾ was purified from beginning to end for this second half, mentioning in it only the Hereafter and what happens in it of the conditions of the earth and its inhabitants, it equals half the Qur'an. It is more fitting then that this hadith be sound, and Allah knows best. For this reason he used to recite these two surahs in the two rak'ahs of the tawaf, and because they are the two surahs of sincerity and tawhid, he would open the day's work with them and close it with them, and recite them in Hajj, which is the emblem of tawhid.
[Chapter on the two tawhids upon which the Book of Allah revolves]
Salvation, felicity and success depend on realising the two tawhids upon which the books of Allah revolve. It was for their realisation that Allah, glorified and exalted, sent His Messenger ﷺ, and to them all the messengers, peace and blessings of Allah be upon them all, from the first of them to the last, called.
The first is scientific, reportive, doctrinal tawhid, which includes affirming the attributes of perfection for Allah, exalted is He, and declaring Him free of likeness and resemblance in them, and declaring Him free of attributes of deficiency.
The second tawhid is worship of Him alone with no partner, singling out love for Him, sincerity towards Him, fear and hope in Him, reliance upon Him, contentment with Him as Lord, God and Guardian, and not making any equal to Him in anything.
He, glorified and exalted, has combined these two kinds of tawhid in the two surahs of sincerity.
They are: the surah ﴿Say: O you disbelievers﴾, which includes practical, volitional tawhid, and the surah ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, which includes reportive, scientific tawhid.
So in the surah ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ is the explanation of what is due to Allah, exalted is He, of attributes of perfection, and the explanation of what must be declared free of Him of deficiencies and likenesses. In the surah ﴿Say: O you disbelievers﴾ is the obligation of worshipping Him alone (with no partner) and disavowal of worship of everything other than Him. Neither of the two tawhids is complete without the other. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ would recite these two surahs in the Sunnah of Fajr, Maghrib and Witr, which are the opening and closing of the work, so that the beginning of the day is tawhid and its end is tawhid.
So scientific, reportive tawhid has two opposites: ta'til (denial of attributes), and tashbih and tamthil (likening). Whoever negates the attributes of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and denies them, his ta'til contradicts his tawhid. Whoever likens Him to His creation and makes Him similar to them, his tashbih and tamthil contradict his tawhid.
Practical, volitional tawhid has two opposites: turning away from love of Him, repentance towards Him, and reliance upon Him, or associating others with Him in that and taking His friends as intercessors besides Him.
Glorified and exalted is He, has combined the two tawhids in more than one place in the Qur'an. Among them is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord who created you and those before you, that you may be righteous. He who made the earth a resting place for you and the sky a canopy, and sent down from the sky water and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not attribute to Allah equals while you know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 21].
Among them is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah is He who made for you the night to rest in and the day as something visible. Indeed Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of the people are not grateful. That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded? Thus are deluded those who used to deny the signs of Allah. Allah is He who made for you the earth a stable place and the sky a ceiling and formed you and perfected your forms and provided for you of the good things. That is Allah, your Lord; so blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds. He is the Living; there is no deity except Him, so invoke Him, sincere to Him in religion. All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [Ghafir: 61].
Among them is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah is He who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days; then He established Himself above the Throne. You have not besides Him any ally or intercessor; so will you not remember? He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth; then it ascends to Him in a Day, the extent of which is a thousand years of what you count. That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Almighty, the Merciful﴾ [al-Sajdah: 4].
(Fa'ida)
Know that among the most noble knowledge is applying negative attributes to the names of Allah, exalted is He.
As for purely negative attributes, they do not enter His descriptions, exalted is He, unless they imply an affirmation, like "the One" (al-Ahad), which implies His singularity in lordship and divinity.
And "al-Salam", which implies His freedom from every deficiency contrary to His perfection. Likewise, reporting about Him by negations is for the affirmation they imply, as in His saying: ﴿Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him﴾, for it implies the perfection of His life and self-subsistence.
Likewise His saying: ﴿And no fatigue touched Us﴾ implies the perfection of His power.
Likewise His saying: ﴿And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of the weight of an atom﴾ implies the perfection of His knowledge.

(Section) Ibn al-Qayyim also said regarding His saying: ﴿He neither begets nor is born﴾ that it includes the perfection of His self-sufficiency (samadiyyah) and His independence.

And likewise His saying: ﴿And there is none comparable to Him﴾ includes His being unique in His perfection and that there is no equal to Him.

(Section) Ibn al-Qayyim said, after some discussion:

Look at the Jahmiyyah and their followers: they approached the blameworthy anthropomorphism (tashbih) and turned away from it altogether, yet they approached perfection and praise and turned them into anthropomorphism and likening (tamthil) — the reverse of what the Qur'an affirms, and which it brings in every respect.

Among this is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And there is none comparable to Him﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 4].

It is a negation, of the creature, of its equivalence to and likeness with the Creator, glorified is He. He did not say, "He is not comparable to anyone," which would negate His resemblance to the creature and His equivalence to it, since that is clearer and more evident than to need negating.

The secret of this: the intent is that the creature does not resemble Him, glorified is He, in any of His attributes and qualities. As for His being, glorified is He, not resembling the creature — not resembling it, not being like it, not being a rival (nid) to it or its equal — there is no praise in that for Him.

For if some king or other person were praised by being said to be unlike animals, stones, wood, and the like, this would not count as praise, nor as commendation of him, nor as a perfection for him. By contrast, if it is said: "Do not set up for the king a rival, an equal, or a likeness among his subjects, [so that] you honour him as he is honoured, and obey him as he is obeyed, for there is no one among his subjects who can rival him, resemble him, or equal him" — this is the utmost praise.

(Subsection) Ibn al-Qayyim said:

I once said to Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, that some scholars had been asked which is more beneficial for the servant: glorification (tasbih) or seeking forgiveness (istighfar)? He said: "If the garment is clean, then incense and rose-water are more beneficial for it; if it is soiled, then soap and hot water are more beneficial for it."

Then he said to me, may Allah have mercy on him: "How, when garments are never free of soiling?"

Within this category is that Surah ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ equals a third of the Qur'an, yet it cannot take the place of the verses on inheritance, divorce, khul', the waiting period ('iddah), and the like. Rather, those verses are more beneficial at their proper time and when needed than the recitation of Surah al-Ikhlas.

Since prayer comprises recitation, remembrance, and supplication, and gathers the parts of servitude in the most complete way, it is superior to each of recitation, remembrance, and supplication taken alone, because it combines all of them together with the servitude of all the limbs.

This is a very beneficial principle that opens for the servant the door of knowing the ranks of deeds and placing them in their proper stations, so that he does not occupy himself with the lesser (mafdul) and thereby lose the greater (fadil) — allowing Iblis to take the difference between them — or look at the greater and occupy himself with it at the expense of the lesser when that is the time for the lesser, so that its benefit is entirely lost, supposing that his occupation with the greater yields more reward and greater recompense.

This requires knowledge of the ranks of deeds, their differences and their objectives, and understanding in giving each deed its due, placing it in its rank, and prioritizing what is more important over it, or prioritizing what is more excellent and superior when what is lesser can be made up for and returned to. If this lesser deed is one that cannot be made up for once missed, then occupying oneself with it takes precedence — such as leaving off recitation to return a greeting or to bless one who sneezes — even though the Qur'an is superior, because one can occupy oneself with this lesser matter and return to the superior one, unlike when one occupies oneself with recitation and misses the benefit of returning the greeting and blessing the sneezer. And so it is with all deeds when they conflict. And Allah, the Exalted, is the Granter of success.

(Chapter) His guidance (ﷺ) in treating the sting of a scorpion with ruqyah

Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in his Musnad, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was praying, he prostrated, and a scorpion stung him on the finger. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned away and said: 'May Allah curse the scorpion, it spares neither a prophet nor anyone else.'" He said: "Then he called for a vessel containing water and salt, and he began placing the place of the sting in the water and salt, reciting: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ and the two protective surahs (al-Mu'awwidhatayn), until it calmed down."

In this hadith is treatment by a remedy combined from two matters: the natural and the divine. For in Surah al-Ikhlas is the perfection of scientific, doctrinal tawhid, and the affirmation of God's oneness (ahadiyyah), which entails the negation of every partner from Him, and the affirmation of self-sufficiency (samadiyyah), which entails the affirmation of every perfection for Him, given that creatures turn to Him in their needs — that is, the creation intends Him and directs itself to Him, both its higher and lower parts — and the negation of a father, a son, and an equal from Him, which includes the negation of origin, branch, peer, and equivalent. These are the things through which it is distinguished and which make it equal to a third of the Qur'an. Thus in His name al-Samad is the affirmation of all perfection, and in the negation of an equal is the transcendence of Him above likeness and similitude. And in al-Ahad is the negation of every partner to the Lord of Majesty. These three foundations are the comprehensive elements of tawhid.

In the two protective surahs is seeking refuge from every disliked thing, in general and in detail. For seeking refuge from the evil of what He created encompasses every evil from which refuge is sought, whether in bodies or in spirits.

Seeking refuge from the evil of the ghasiq, which is the night, and its sign, which is the moon when it sets, includes seeking refuge from the evil of what spreads within it of wicked spirits, which the light of day used to prevent from spreading; when the night darkened over them and the moon set, they spread out and wrought corruption.

Seeking refuge from the evil of the blowers in knots includes seeking refuge from the evil of sorceresses and their sorcery.

Seeking refuge from the evil of the envier includes seeking refuge from wicked souls that harm by their envy and their evil eye.

The second surah includes seeking refuge from the evil of the devils of mankind and jinn. Thus the two surahs together comprise seeking refuge from every evil, and they have a great standing in guarding and fortifying against evils before they occur. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) instructed ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir to recite them after every prayer; al-Tirmidhi mentioned it in his Jami'. In this is a great secret for warding off evils from one prayer to the next. He said: "The seekers of refuge have never sought refuge with the like of these two." It has been mentioned that he (ﷺ) was bewitched with eleven knots, and that Jibril descended to him with them, and every time he recited a verse from them a knot came undone, until all the knots were undone, and it was as though he had been freed from a fetter.
